html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. API: application programming interface; YAML: a human-readable data format for configuration

  • The CLAUDE.md hierarchy: user, project and directory level, and who shares what
  • @import and .claude/rules/ to keep instructions modular; /memory to diagnose
  • Slash commands and skills: where they live, and the frontmatter context: fork, allowed-tools, argument-hint
  • Path-specific rules with glob patterns, and when they beat directory-level files

2CLAUDE.md Files and Their Hierarchy (Task 3.1)

Running case

A New Engineer at Birchwood Supply Gets Different Answers

  • A teammate joins and Claude Code ignores the team's coding standards
  • The standards sit in the lead developer's own ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md
  • Another problem: the root file has grown to 800 lines, mixing testing, API and deployment rules

CLAUDE.md is a Markdown file of persistent instructions that Claude Code loads into context at the start of a session.

Level Location Shared with the team?
User ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md No: applies only to you, not in version control
Project CLAUDE.md at the repo root, or .claude/CLAUDE.md Yes, through version control
Directory CLAUDE.md inside a subdirectory Yes (committed); applies to work in that directory

  • Diagnosis rule: a new teammate not receiving instructions usually means those instructions live in user-level configuration instead of project-level configuration.
  • Files are combined, not overridden: more specific content is simply added to the context. Keep each file short (the guidance is under about 200 lines) and avoid contradictions.

Keeping it modular

  • @import: reference other files from a CLAUDE.md so each package pulls in only the standards that apply to it (for example @docs/standards/testing.md). Paths resolve relative to the file that contains the import.
  • .claude/rules/: split a large CLAUDE.md into topic files such as testing.md, api-conventions.md, deployment.md.
  • /memory shows which memory files are loaded and lets you open them: use it to diagnose inconsistent behavior across sessions.
Exam tip

"Instructions apply for me but not for a teammate" → user vs project level. "One huge file" → split into .claude/rules/ topic files or @import.

[Verify live] Current documentation adds: a CLAUDE.local.md for private project preferences (gitignored); managed policy CLAUDE.md for organizations; CLAUDE.md files in directories above the working directory load at launch while those in subdirectories load on demand when Claude works with files there; imports can nest up to four levels. CLAUDE.md is context, not enforcement: for guaranteed behavior use hooks (Module 3). As of 8 November 2026.

3Slash Commands and Skills (Task 3.2)

Project-scoped User-scoped
Custom slash command .claude/commands/ (in the repo, shared when teammates clone or pull) ~/.claude/commands/ (personal)
Skill .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md (shared) ~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md (personal)

A skill is a folder with a SKILL.md file: YAML frontmatter plus instructions, used on demand for a task-specific workflow.

---
name: analyze-codebase
description: Map modules and dependencies of a package and report findings
context: fork
allowed-tools: Read, Grep, Glob
argument-hint: "[package-name]"
---
Analyze the package $ARGUMENTS. List its modules, public interfaces and dependencies.
Return a short summary only.
Frontmatter What it does
context: fork Runs the skill in an isolated sub-agent context, so verbose output (codebase analysis) or exploratory context (brainstorming alternatives) does not pollute the main conversation
allowed-tools Restricts tool access during skill execution (for example only file-write or read-only tools) to avoid destructive actions
argument-hint Prompts the developer for required parameters when they invoke the skill without arguments

  • Personal variants: to customize a team skill for yourself, create your own in ~/.claude/skills/ with a different name, so teammates are unaffected.

Skills versus CLAUDE.md

CLAUDE.md Skill or command
Loaded Always On demand, when invoked (or chosen by Claude for a matching task)
Use for Universal standards that apply to nearly every task Task-specific workflows (review checklist, release steps, migrations)

[Verify live] [Old name] In current Claude Code, custom commands have been merged into skills: a file at .claude/commands/deploy.md and a skill at .claude/skills/deploy/SKILL.md both create /deploy; existing command files keep working, and if both exist the skill wins. Note that allowed-tools pre-approves the listed tools (no permission prompt) and does not by itself forbid other tools; use disallowedTools or permission rules to restrict. Skill descriptions are always in context; the full content loads when the skill is used. As of 8 November 2026. For the exam, answer as the guide teaches (commands in .claude/commands/, allowed-tools to limit tools).

Exam tip

Always-needed standards go in CLAUDE.md; task workflows go in skills or commands; verbose or exploratory skills use context: fork.

4Path-Specific Rules (Task 3.3)

Problem: coding conventions differ by area (React components, API handlers, database models) and test files sit next to the code they test throughout the repository. A directory-level CLAUDE.md cannot cover files spread across many directories.

Solution: put rule files in .claude/rules/ with YAML frontmatter paths holding glob patterns. The rule loads only when Claude works with a matching file.

---
paths:
  - "**/*.test.tsx"
  - "**/*.test.ts"
---
# Testing conventions
- Use React Testing Library queries by role, not by test id.
- One behavior per test; name tests "it ... when ...".

Choice Best when
Path-specific rule (paths: globs) Conventions follow file type or pattern, spread across directories (all test files), and should apply automatically and deterministically
Directory-level CLAUDE.md Conventions belong to one directory tree
Skill A workflow the developer invokes on demand; not automatic by file path
One big root CLAUDE.md Small projects; unreliable when areas differ (relies on the model inferring which section applies)
  • Advantages: less irrelevant context and fewer tokens, because the rule is absent until needed.
Exam tip

Conventions tied to file type and scattered across directories (tests) call for path-specific rules with globs, not many directory CLAUDE.md files.

5Exam Q&A

S1A new engineer says Claude Code does not follow the team's standards, but it does for the lead developer. The lead put the standards in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md. What is the fix?

  • ARe-run /init on the new engineer's laptop only
  • BMove the standards into the project CLAUDE.md and commit it
  • CAsk the new engineer to copy the lead's home directory
  • DAdd the standards to each developer's ~/.claude/commands/ folder as a command
Show the answer

Answer: B. User-level files apply only to that user; project-level files travel with the repository.

S2A root CLAUDE.md has grown to 800 lines covering testing, API design and deployment. Which change keeps instructions maintainable?

  • ADelete the file
  • BSplit it into topic files under .claude/rules/ (testing.md, api-conventions.md)
  • CMove everything into the user-level file so that it no longer clutters the repository root
  • DAdd more headings and keep one file
Show the answer

Answer: B. Topic-specific rule files give a modular alternative to a monolithic file.

S3A monorepo has packages that each need different standards documents. How can each package's CLAUDE.md include only the right ones?

  • ACopy and paste the documents into every package file so each one is self-contained
  • BUse @import to pull the relevant standards files into each package's CLAUDE.md
  • CRename the documents to CLAUDE.md
  • DPut all standards in the user-level file
Show the answer

Answer: B. @import pulls in selected files and keeps each file modular.

S4Claude behaves differently between two sessions on the same repository. How can you check what instructions were loaded?

  • ADelete the .claude directory and start again with a clean configuration
  • BAsk the model to guess which files it loaded in the earlier session
  • CReinstall Claude Code
  • DRun /memory to see which memory files are loaded
Show the answer

Answer: D. /memory shows the loaded memory files and helps diagnose inconsistency.

S5The team wants a /release-check command that runs its standard release checklist and should be available to every developer who clones the repository. Where should the command file go?

  • A~/.claude/commands/ on one laptop
  • BThe root CLAUDE.md as a paragraph
  • C.claude/commands/ in the project repository
  • DA hidden file in each developer's home directory
Show the answer

Answer: C. Project-scoped commands in the repository are version-controlled and shared.

S6A skill that analyzes a whole codebase prints thousands of lines and clutters the main conversation. Which frontmatter helps?

  • Aargument-hint
  • BA longer description
  • Ccontext: fork
  • Dname
Show the answer

Answer: C. context: fork runs the skill in an isolated context and returns only its summary.

S7A skill needs a required package name but developers often run it with no argument. Which option prompts for it?

  • Acontext: fork
  • Ballowed-tools
  • Cpaths
  • Dargument-hint
Show the answer

Answer: D. argument-hint shows what parameter is expected when the skill is invoked without arguments.

S8A developer wants a personal variation of a shared skill without changing it for teammates. What should they do?

  • ADelete the shared skill
  • BEdit the shared skill in the repository and ask teammates to ignore the change
  • CCreate a personal skill in ~/.claude/skills/ under a different name
  • DRename the repository
Show the answer

Answer: C. A personal skill under a different name leaves teammates unaffected.

S9Test files (*.test.tsx) sit next to components all over the codebase, and all of them must follow the same testing conventions automatically. What is the most maintainable setup?

  • AA rule file in .claude/rules/ with paths: ["**/*.test.tsx"]
  • BA skill that the developer remembers to run
  • CAdd a CLAUDE.md in every directory that holds tests
  • DOne root CLAUDE.md with a testing section and hope Claude infers when it applies
Show the answer

Answer: A. Glob-scoped rules apply by file pattern wherever the files are and load only when needed.

S10Which content belongs in the always-loaded CLAUDE.md, not in a skill?

  • AA brainstorming workflow for architecture decisions that engineers start on demand
  • BA release checklist that is used by the team only twice a year
  • CUniversal coding standards that apply to nearly every task
  • DA one-off migration script
Show the answer

Answer: C. Always-loaded context is for universal standards; task-specific workflows suit on-demand skills.

S11Which TWO statements about path-specific rules are correct? Select TWO.

  • AThey only work for one directory
  • BThey load when Claude works with a matching file
  • CThey load for every file at all times
  • DThey must be run as a slash command
  • EThey use frontmatter paths with glob patterns
Show the answer

Answer: B, E. A glob in the rule's frontmatter scopes it to matching files wherever they are, and it loads only when needed. It is not limited to one directory and needs no command.

S12Which TWO belong in the user-level ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md? Select TWO.

  • AThe shared testing rules of the repository
  • BYour personal preferences, such as how you like explanations
  • CThe repository-wide release steps
  • DThe team coding standards new teammates must follow
  • EYour own shortcuts and habits
Show the answer

Answer: B, E. User-level instructions are personal and not shared. Standards, testing rules and release steps for the team belong at project level.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Levels User ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md (personal) · Project CLAUDE.md/.claude/CLAUDE.md (shared) · Directory subfolder files
Modular @import · .claude/rules/*.md topic files · /memory to see what loaded
Commands Project .claude/commands/ (shared) vs user ~/.claude/commands/ (personal)
Skills .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md; frontmatter context: fork, allowed-tools, argument-hint
Personal variant Own skill in ~/.claude/skills/ under a different name
Skill vs CLAUDE.md Skill = on demand, task-specific; CLAUDE.md = always loaded, universal
Path rules .claude/rules/x.md with paths: globs (e.g. **/*.test.tsx); loads only for matching files; beats directory files for spread-out conventions
